races.name: British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Jimmy Loxam Is 80 Today "Confined" Handicap (For horses Which Have Not Won In 2026 Flat Turf Season)

runners_data.name: Wen Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist dropping back to 5f where they won last time on soft; Ben Haslam yard in decent 14-day form (2/14), 19 days fresh, and the sim-going record is competent — the main concern is whether a genuinely slow pace suits a closer at this course.

runners_data.name: Storm Call
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good ground in their form string and returns after 90 days off for the Easterbys; the layoff is a note of caution but the 5f good-ground form reads well and barrier/jockey experience of Joanna Mason on a straight track is a positive.

runners_data.name: Polka
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse whose true style is closer than the midfield map position reflects; the 128-day absence is significant, headgear includes a hood, and while the one win came over 5f on standard they have limited recent good-ground evidence — racing out of preferred role compounds the fitness query.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Back quickly (12 days) for Adrian Nicholls who is represented at modest but consistent 14-day strike rate; genuinely strong sim-going profile (12/15) with two wins and three places at 5f, but as a natural hold-up horse mapped forward it will need a strong pace that this race shape probably won't deliver.

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and sole pace-setter in the race, giving it a structural gift on a flat straight five; OR 64 is the lowest in the field and the sim-going record is thin (3 runs, no wins or places), but freedom from front means it cannot be dismissed as an each-way outsider at a price.

runners_data.name: Woodhay Whisper
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse wearing headgear (h) with a very slim sim-going record (1/15) — the fast Catterick ground is a live concern; Ron Barr sends this runner back quickly (17 days) and the recent form figures (1,8,7,4,9,7) offer little confidence in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Albegone
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's hold-up runner returns just six days after its last start, headgear includes a hood and blinkers; the 5f good-ground sim-going profile is reasonable (9/15, two places) and David Allan is an experienced pilot, but as a natural closer mapped to midfield the uncontested pace will blunt its finishing kick.

races.paceDynamic: Our Absent Friends is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner sprint and, with no genuine challenger for the early lead, should bowl along uncontested at a sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Catterick's straight five. That steady, controlled tempo heavily favours horses who can track the pace and quicken from a prominent position rather than those needing a strong, end-to-end gallop to close into. The field is stacked with hold-up types — Polka, Tees Aggregates, Woodhay Whisper and Albegone are all natural closers who have been redistributed forward on the map simply because there is nowhere else to put them, meaning the genuine rear-of-field challenge will be diluted and competitive. This shape overwhelmingly favours prominent-to-midfield horses who can latch onto the leader's slipstream and sprint clear in the final furlong, with true hold-up horses at a structural disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Our Absent Friends has a completely unchallenged lead — watch whether Shane Gray exploits the gift by going notably fast early or conserves energy; either choice dramatically reshapes the finish.

Polka and Albegone are both equipped with headgear and are natural hold-up horses who will be hunting room in a tight seven-runner field down the straight — congestion between them in the final two furlongs is a real risk.

Storm Call returns from 90 days off and has not been seen since a standard-ground run; watch early market moves for signs the Easterbys have done enough work at home to justify confidence on the fast surface.

The Going Report confirms 5f at Catterick as Good to Firm — Woodhay Whisper has only one sim-going data point from 15 runs and should be treated with caution if considered in any scenario requiring fast-ground hold-up ability.

Tees Aggregates runs just 12 days after its last outing and Adrian Nicholls keeps a tight team — watch paddock condition and whether the horse moves with freshness, as a flat, uncontested gallop at this trip will test whether it can produce its best closing effort from a compromised position.

races.name: Catterick Racecourse Supporting Racing Staff Week Handicap

runners_data.name: Thehunnebelllegacy
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with modest placed form, no wins from nine runs on similar going and just 3 finishes in the first three from those; Ethan Tindall claims 5lb off a modest OR=55 but the 32-day break and poor sim-going record offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Elashgar
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: sole confirmed front-runner who set fractions to suit on its one win over this C&D equivalent trip; Conor Whiteley takes 7lb off, 57-day absence is the only flag, and the style-fit tag reflects that dictating is its role not a departure from it.

runners_data.name: Rivera Queen
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse carrying a tongue-tie back after a 13-day turnaround; shifted onto the pace map because the rear is over-subscribed, though its one placed run came at 6f on good ground suggesting ability to run well if the race falls right — style penalty applies.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Wears a p (hood/hood or similar) for the first time in handicap company; hold-up type whose five sim-going runs produced no wins or places, and the Jack Nicholls 5lb claim is the main hook, though the headgear could sharpen its early effort and push it forward.

runners_data.name: Our Hero Matty
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's gelding is a genuine hold-up type who has been mapped closer than it naturally races; recent efforts over 5f produced double-figures finishes and the step to 6f with Barry McHugh aboard is a positive, but form figures of 0-0 in the last two starts demand caution regardless of shape.

runners_data.name: Long Shot
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's consistent operator holds 2 places from 8 runs on similar ground and most recently ran 4th off OR=51 at this trip — David Allan rides and the horse is best served tracking the pace at close range, making it one of the likelier beneficiaries if Elashgar rolls along in front.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes the ride on a filly with four consecutive seconds at 6f across soft and good ground — the record shows genuine consistency at this trip and Fallon's experience makes her a strong candidate to produce a late challenge in a shape where the pace is set and she can time her run.

races.paceDynamic: Elashgar is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 6f handicap and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the gate on good to firm ground at Catterick. The remainder of the field — Rivera Queen, Our Hero Matty, Long Shot, and Battenburg Belle — are all genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map purely because there are too many closers for the rear to accommodate them all; the horses most likely to actually secure a forward position behind Elashgar are Long Shot and Saxon Grace, given their in-running tendencies and draw. With one horse controlling from the front at a pace it chooses, and the back half of the field carrying multiple horses racing out of role, this race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can track Elashgar at close range and challenge in the final furlong, rather than genuine hold-up horses launching from the back.

watchPoints.text: Battenburg Belle has four consecutive second-place finishes at 6f and Cieren Fallon is the standout booking — monitor whether she gets a clean run from a potentially congested midfield group given the redistribution.
Elashgar has not run for 57 days; watch the pre-race paddock — any signs of rustiness or freshness in the market could reframe whether it truly controls the pace or gives it up early.

Saxon Grace is reported in headgear for the first time — if the gear sharpens its early pace it could push closer to Elashgar than expected and create a two-horse lead scenario that changes the shape of the race.

Long Shot's most recent two runs were over 7f on good ground where it finished 4th and 2nd respectively — dropping back to 6f today could mean it settles closer to the pace than its listed hold-up style suggests, worth noting for positioning.

The going is reported Good To Firm at 6f, faster than some runners in this field have recent form on — Rivera Queen and Our Hero Matty both have sim-going records showing limited impact on quick surfaces, which tempers their hold-up threat further.

races.name: Congratulations To The Happy Couple EBF Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Diamont Katie
runners_data.note: Recent winner over this trip on Good ground gives her strong credentials as the race-shaper; Jack Nicholls (5lb claim) retains the ride for K R Burke, who has been in excellent form at 10/48 over 14 days; her style fit at the front is high and she is the key tactical reference point for the entire race.

runners_data.name: Alessia Fernanda
runners_data.note: Zak Wheatley partners this six-year-old for Declan Carroll, whose yard is in modest recent form (1/10 over 14 days); sole course form entry is at 8f and headgear (tongue-tie) is retained, but her winning form came over a mile on Standfast ground and this 7f flat track on faster ground looks a slight step into the unknown.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Queen
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up mare for the Fahey yard who has struggled badly at this trip on Good ground (8th, 9th) in her last two starts; Ethan Tindall takes over on a 5lb claim, which helps her mark, but her similar-going form is bare (0W0P) and she needs the pace to be genuine to produce her best.

runners_data.name: In A Hurry
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is a powerful booking for David O'Meara, but this genuine hold-up filly — who has finished 8th, 9th and 9th in her last three at this trip — finds herself squeezed into a midfield role by the volume of hold-up types; her style-fit tag reflects she will not get the true off-the-pace setup she needs, and recent form at this trip on Good ground is deeply uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's three-year-old has a smart placed record over 7f on Good ground (two 2nds from five attempts) and races prominently with headgear (p) fitted; Ben Robinson keeps the ride, the yard is winless over 14 days (0/19) which is a flag, but the horse's profile suits this scenario well if she can track Diamont Katie closely.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's three-year-old arrives on a short seven-day turnaround carrying 127lbs but boasts two recent 7f wins on Good ground and rates among the most in-form runners in the race; Rowan Scott rides and her prominent style is a tactical asset in what shapes as a slowly-run affair — form figures of 1,1 over this trip and going are the most relevant in the field.

runners_data.name: Yorkshire Queen
runners_data.note: Grant Tuer's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up type whose best recent form (3rd, 2nd) came over shorter trips on Standfast and Good ground; Clifford Lee rides, but the horse's redistribution to midfield in this map means she is unlikely to get the patient, late-delivery setup her form demands, and her record over 7f on Good ground (3rd best effort) offers modest hope at best.

races.paceDynamic: Diamont Katie is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to push her hard from the outset, she should be able to set a controlled, sustainable gallop over Catterick's flat 7f on going that is effectively Good to Firm. Homestrait and Velvet Rhythm will press forward into prominent positions and keep her honest, but neither is a natural leader, so the pace is unlikely to be truly strong. In A Hurry and Yorkshire Queen are genuine hold-up horses who have been mapped into midfield purely because the race has too many runners seeking the rear — neither is truly likely to get a late-run setup from an orthodox position, and their effective running style in this race will be closer to midfield than genuine off-the-pace. This race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or press from just off the leader, as a moderate, controllable gallop on fast ground at Catterick over 7f is unlikely to produce a true closing opportunity for deep hold-up types.

scenarios.body: If Diamont Katie dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and kicks clear from 2f out on the fast ground.

watchPoints.text: Velvet Rhythm's two recent wins over 7f on Good ground make her the most dangerous prominent challenger to Diamont Katie — watch whether Rowan Scott positions her immediately behind the leader from the outset.

In A Hurry and Yorkshire Queen are genuine hold-up horses being forced into midfield by race shape — if either struggles to settle or gets pushed wide early, their already slim chances are effectively extinguished.
Homestrait's trainer Brian Ellison is winless in 19 runners over the past 14 days — flag this as a potential negative form angle before committing to the horse's strong placed profile.

The going is effectively Good to Firm despite the card listing Good — watch for any horse that has a going concern on faster ground, particularly Alessia Fernanda whose winning form came on Standfast and Soft.
With Diamont Katie's handler K R Burke in sharp 14-day form (10/48), any drift in her price in the market early would be a significant signal to monitor given her control of the pace map.

races.name: Start Your Racing TV Free Trial Handicap

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old hold-up type for Martin Todhunter, David Nolan takes the ride 22 days after a course run over 2m on good ground where he finished 6th; similar-going record of 1W4P from 15 runs shows consistency without dominance, and the 2-mile trip suits his stamina but he needs pace to chase.|

runners_data.name: Treasure Islands
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old arrives on the back of a recent win over this trip on good ground and carries a trainer 13/106 14-day strike rate; David Allan rides and, as the sole pace-setter in a 4-runner field, she owns the race shape entirely — her OR=70 is the joint-highest and her ability to dictate is this race's defining factor.|

runners_data.name: Valley Of Flowers
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason partners this 8-year-old for the Coward yard, who have no 14-day runners logged; a hold-up type whose similar-going record of 0W4P from 15 runs suggests placed reliability rather than a winning threat, and the 2m trip on good to firm is within her range based on a recent 2nd over 12f on good.|

runners_data.name: Twilight Safari
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's 4-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but the field's clustering of rear-runners means it is mapped forward of its true position; 36 days since last run and a form string of 6-4-6-7-0 offer little encouragement, and the style-fit discount of 0.90 reflects that racing out of its natural role further diminishes its prospects here.|

races.paceDynamic: Treasure Islands is the lone confirmed front-runner in a field of just four, and with no genuine challenger for the lead over this 2-mile trip at Catterick, she will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on good to firm ground. Arrange and Valley Of Flowers are both hold-up types by inclination, while Twilight Safari — a true hold-up operator — has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can accommodate, meaning the genuine closing positions are crowded and Twilight Safari is unlikely to get its natural position freely. With one horse owning the pace and setting a measured tempo unchallenged, the race will likely be run to suit those who can travel prominently or make a sustained move from the middle pack, rather than those relying on a strong late injection from off the pace. This race shape firmly favours a prominent or patient-but-handy profile that can respond when Treasure Islands quickens from the front on fast ground, rather than a deep hold-up ride.

watchPoints.text: Treasure Islands is the sole pace-maker in a 4-runner field — if she is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at her own pace, she may simply never be headed and the tactical map resolves instantly in her favour.

Arrange's hold-up style is under pressure in this race shape — David Nolan will need to position him closer than his natural inclination to have any chance of landing a telling blow over the 2-mile trip.

Twilight Safari's 36-day absence combined with a form line of 6-4-6-7-0 and a redistribution out of its true style makes it a significant underdog — monitor whether Jack Nicholls elects to push it forward early, which would signal a change of tactics.
Valley Of Flowers' trainer Samantha & Jacqueline Coward have zero runners in the 14-day window — watch for any market support as a signal of stable confidence given limited public data.

With only four runners, the field is thin enough that any early incident or pace collapse would scramble the entire race shape — a false start, stumble, or sudden bunching in the back straight could make all pre-race pace profiling redundant.

races.name: Racing Again 8th July Handicap

runners_data.name: Sanditon
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with five consecutive 7f runs at Sandown under Charlie Johnston's yard, which has been hitting form (6 wins from 52 in 14 days); Good to Firm going is ticked, but no Catterick form and a wide draw could make the tight finish tricky.|

runners_data.name: Emerald Army
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's sole runner here, freshened up on just six days' rest, and holds the critical role of sole front-runner; sim-going record of 0 wins from 4 places suggests she finds it hard to convert, and the STYLE_FIT tag flags she may not be fully in her preferred mode, so watch for her to get caught late.|

runners_data.name: Captain Cess
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who has placed at 6f on Good and Soft, but his 7f record shows trips over a mile and longer have left him mid-division; Zak Wheatley takes over and a step back from 8f could suit, though the Good to Firm surface is untested over this trip.|

runners_data.name: Classy Clarets
runners_data.note: The form horse of the race with a 5f win and multiple places on Good ground, and headgear (h) suggests she needs a positive ride; David Nolan is an astute booking for Iain Jardine, and her 7f Goodish-ground place confirms the trip and surface combination is viable.|

runners_data.name: War Memorial
runners_data.note: Conor Whiteley (7) takes the mount and the horse carries a genuine hold-up profile — bumped to midfield on the map simply because the rear is oversubscribed — with one 7f win on Good being the standout piece of form; trainer Mullaney has had zero from three in the last 14 days, which tempers expectations.|

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: The most experienced runner in the field at nine years of age, Rain Cap's prominent style earns him a natural position tracking Emerald Army, and his Stamina form over 7f on similar surfaces (1W5P) makes him competitive; headgear (v) is retained and the five-pound claimer Tindall keeps the weight manageable.|

runners_data.name: Blue Jay Way
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard and has placed on Good, but his true hold-up profile means he is squeezed into a midfield berth that suits him less than a patient ride from the rear would; Mikkel Mortensen (5) is an unfamiliar booking and the STYLE_FIT discount is meaningful here.|

runners_data.name: Misemerald
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's horse has shown nothing in recent form (60-066) and the step back from 8-9f has not helped previously; a natural hold-up type displaced to midfield, and with 32 days off and no win or place on similar going in seven tries, the evidence is firmly against.|

runners_data.name: Martin's Brig
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran whose last five runs all read 6th-to-9th over 7-8f, and headgear (b) has not unlocked any improvement; slotted into midfield despite being a genuine hold-up type, his best Going to Firm run produced a single win but that came a long time ago, and David Thompson's yard has been quiet.|

runners_data.name: Wath Court
runners_data.note: The most concerning runner in the field — raced just two days ago, fades in finishes (flagged explicitly), and has zero wins or places from six recent tries on Good going; Philip Kirby saddles him alongside Misemerald but the condensed turnaround on fast ground over a trip longer than his recent 8-12f efforts makes this very difficult to support.|

races.paceDynamic: Emerald Army is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 7f Catterick handicap on Good to Firm ground and is likely to stride into a comfortable, uncontested lead from the outset, setting a sustainable rather than pressurised gallop. Rain Cap is the only other genuine prominent type and will track closely, meaning the front two set a controlled tempo with no rivalry sufficient to burn them out. The bulk of this field — Sanditon, Captain Cess, Classy Clarets, War Memorial, Blue Jay Way, Misemerald, Martin's Brig, and Wath Court — are all natural hold-up or off-pace horses, but several (War Memorial, Blue Jay Way, Misemerald, Martin's Brig, Wath Court) have been redistributed onto the map because the field contains far more true hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; in reality, some of these will be forced wider and closer to the pace than they would choose. With a single, unhurried pace-setter operating at a controlled clip, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine late kick — particularly those with proven form at 7f on Good or Good to Firm ground who can produce a clean sustained run into the straight — but only those whose redistribution has not compromised their true profile.

watchPoints.text: Emerald Army's ability to hold on — watch whether Rain Cap applies any pressure in the opening two furlongs, as even minor competition for the lead could see Emerald Army's uncontested advantage disappear and the race open up for hold-up horses.|

Traffic danger in the final furlong is elevated: five genuinely held-up horses (War Memorial, Blue Jay Way, Misemerald, Martin's Brig, Wath Court) have all been forced closer than ideal, and Catterick's tight final turn makes it very easy for a clustered midfield to get boxed in — watch for gaps.|

Wath Court raced only two days ago and carries a 'fades in finish' flag; if Philip Kirby runs both his horses prominently out of necessity, Misemerald and Wath Court could compromise each other's runs in the straight.|

Classy Clarets' headgear (h) combined with David Nolan's positive front-of-midfield style could see her asked for effort earlier than her natural hold-up profile suggests — watch whether she gets into a rhythm around the bend or gets shuffled back in the pack.|

War Memorial's 7f Good-ground win is the form line to keep onside in this race shape, but Conor Whiteley's 7lb claim means the horse carries less weight than rivals — watch whether he can secure a clean position on the outside of the pack when the field begins to tighten entering the home straight.|
